title: Actor-side components of dyadic event forecasts: an ownership decomposition, specification dependence, and a matched-vintage audit in a 196-actor ICEWS panel
description: Public artifact and L0-L2 verification release for the V2 manuscript on actor-side components of dyadic event forecasts in a 196-actor ICEWS panel, 1995-2023. The release ships code, tests, the V1 confirmatory and stability aggregates, and the V2 matched-vintage aggregate tree. The analysis applies a post-hoc six-class ownership convention to a plan-declared feature list, fixes unit and sign, and makes every logistic forecast carry an exact group-additive decomposition into source-role, target-role, dyad and non-actor groups; the ownership convention has no pre-run record. It is a design convention and audit, not a new estimator (the decomposition is the logistic identity and coincides with linear SHAP under a training-mean background). The V2 recomputation gives 45.2% actor-owned and 54.8% not actor-owned; only 4 of 49 features are role-specific. The V1 49-feature model loses to a 2017-vintage warm baseline on the one-shot unit-fresh 20% dyad holdout (0.217875 vs 0.209729 log-loss). A post-hoc matched-vintage audit on the same burned holdout finds that the 47-feature model beats a 2014-vintage warm baseline by 0.020954 (95% CI 0.015443-0.026465), a 25-feature model with no actor-owned column beats it by 0.017743, and the 22 added columns contribute 0.003211. The as-specified 49 is null against the matched comparator under the H0 cache. V2 is post hoc and secondary; the V1 49-feature result remains the plan-declared primary. The release is one paper path, not a reusable framework, and is executable at L0-L2 only. Includes the plan-declared (internally hash-timestamped; pre-specified split) one-shot unit-fresh 20% dyad-holdout evaluation (retrospective, not time-fresh), aggregate results, the V2 matched-vintage aggregate tree, and a repository-only illustrative world-line preview (four anchors by 20 non-random sampled dyads, not analysed in the manuscript, no paper result). The within-panel stability audit is provisional, holdout-row-excluded and based on 50 dyad-cluster bootstrap refits; the public experiment scripts are a five-seed preview and do not regenerate those aggregates, and the restricted 50-refit audit code is not redistributed. ICEWS data, row-level predictions, fitted coefficients and labels are not redistributed. No general claim is made about graph features, persistence or any corpus beyond this panel. Source code is MIT-licensed; ICEWS-derived aggregate results are not MIT and remain under the ICEWS research-and-teaching terms. This is the v0.1.1 archival release; no DOI has been minted.
